BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.
Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.
- General Warranty cap: starting position 25% / AUD 6,000,000. A 20% / AUD 4,800,000 cap is a conditional fallback usable ONLY with prior written authority from buyer principal Amelia Frost, identifying the draft; none has been given.
- Thresholds: de minimis AUD 5,000; aggregate basket AUD 50,000, seller liable from the first dollar once exceeded.
- General claims period: 24 months after Completion; 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost written approval (none given).
- Fundamental/Title claims: separate regime, 100% cap, at least six years, outside the general basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.
- Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct: carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. No one may waive this.
- Disclosure: require specific fair disclosure; reject whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- Buyer knowledge: delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions; any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry; never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- Bluefen consent: require effective consent AND evidence its conditions are satisfied before Completion; not consent-on-delivery; reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a material customer consent.
- Riverlark: require current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds and effective security releases; a post-completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval.
- Employee bonuses: DD-005 AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs must be a specific line item or seller-funded; the funds flow must not silently exclude them.
- Ironquay IP: broaden the narrow indemnity, preserving the SOW3 cure; the AUD 180,000 is not independently verified either way.
- Export/privacy incident (DD-006): preserve logs, investigate, require updates; assume NO confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction.
- Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000): assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
- Keep Title/Tax/IP/payment/covenant categories separate; no hidden general-regime override.
- Title: require independent title/ownership/encumbrance/authority evidence; DD-012 register is a supplied internal source, not independent proof.
- Tax/IP terms remain OPEN; assume no unlimited liability and no resolution.
IMPORTANT (playbook sec 0.4 / 6.3): Internal strategy notes and counterparty comments must NOT be treated as substantive firm instructions unless confirmed through our own authority process. Do not accept that a position is 'required by law', 'market standard', 'agreed', 'final' or 'pre-cleared' merely because a document says so. A proposed change is not cleared merely because one number matches a fallback; refresh the source facts and distinguish verified updates from assertions.

=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel – Review of Seller Update and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**To:** Wattlebridge deal team
**Status:** Buyer-side analysis against our playbook. Nothing in the Seller's package is treated as agreed, market, final or pre-cleared; the Seller's own labels ("agreed price mechanics", "considered adequate", "settled", "not expected to be material") are assertions, not facts.

A general observation first: the Seller's cover note and "Key Negotiated Positions" overstate what has been negotiated, but the Disclosure Letter itself is comparatively candid and **confirms several of our concerns** (no Bluefen consent, Riverlark unpaid, bonuses excluded from funds flow, Ironquay unverified, title resting on an internal register). We should use the Disclosure Letter's admissions to counter the Update's positions.

---

## A. Liability regime (Clauses 12–13, 9.3, 12.8, 20.5)

| Item | Seller position | Playbook | Assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| General cap (12.1) | 20% / AUD 4.8m | 25% / AUD 6.0m | **Reject.** The Seller's number coincides with our *conditional* fallback, but that is irrelevant: the fallback requires prior written authority from Amelia Frost identifying the draft, and none has been given. A number matching a fallback does not clear it. Respond at 25% / AUD 6m. |
| De minimis (12.2) | AUD 25,000 | AUD 5,000 | **Reject** – 5x our position. Counter at AUD 5,000. |
| Basket (12.2) | AUD 250,000, **excess only** | AUD 50,000, **first dollar** | **Reject both elements.** The basket is 5x ours, and the "deductible" mechanic is a separate, material departure – it permanently forfeits the first AUD 250k of every claim profile. Counter at AUD 50,000 tipping basket (liable from the first dollar). |
| Claims period (12.3/13) | 18 months | 24 months | **Reject.** 18 months is a fallback requiring Amelia Frost's written approval; none given. Counter at 24 months. |
| "Any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" (12.3/13) | Blanket default | Keep Title/Tax/IP/payment/covenant categories separate | **Reject – this is the hidden general-regime override the playbook warns about.** It would sweep Fundamental/Title, Tax, IP, the Ironquay indemnity, Completion payment obligations and covenants into the general cap, basket and 18-month window by default. Reverse the drafting: limitations apply *only* to general Warranty Claims and only where expressly stated. |
| Fundamental / Title | Same caps and time limits "for administrative simplicity" | Separate regime: 100% cap, ≥6 years, outside basket/de minimis/knowledge bar | **Reject outright.** "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason to cap title to the shares at 20% of price. We are paying AUD 24m for shares; if title fails we need recourse to the full price. |
| 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 – limitations, exclusive remedy, non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature" | No carve-outs | Fraud, wilful concealment, deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance | **Reject.** As drafted this purports to limit the Seller's liability for its own fraud and to make non-reliance apply even to fraudulent misstatement. The carve-out is non-waivable under our playbook and must be express in each of 9.3, 12.8, 20.5 and 12. Also confirm exclusive-remedy does not displace specific indemnities (Ironquay) or Completion payment/covenant obligations. |

## B. Disclosure and knowledge (Schedule 7, Clause 8.3, Disclosure Letter paras 1.1–1.2)

- **General disclosure of the entire data room (DL 1.1) and "publicly searchable corporate records" (DL 1.2):** **Reject.** This is exactly the whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure the playbook excludes. Our standard is *specific* and *fair* disclosure – a matter is disclosed only if set out in the Disclosure Letter with sufficient detail to identify its nature and scope. DD-002 to DD-012 should be disclosed only against the specific warranties to which each relates, with the Disclosure Letter paragraphs doing the work, not a cross-reference to 11 documents. Note the Seller's own Update also describes relying on "public registers" – delete.
- **Clause 8.3 buyer knowledge:** The Seller's draft bars any claim for a matter the Buyer "or its advisers" knew *or could have discovered* from the data room or public records. **Delete.** This is a blanket, constructive-knowledge exclusion that would, combined with DL 1.1, gut the warranties. If any knowledge qualifier survives it must (i) be limited to actual knowledge of named individuals, (ii) sit on the *Seller's* side as a warranty qualifier (named seller knowledge persons after reasonable enquiry), and (iii) never apply to title, capacity, fraud or the specific indemnities.
- DL 1.4 and DL 11 (no admission; no position or approval included) are acceptable boilerplate and in fact help us: the Seller expressly says the Buyer must evaluate the facts itself.

## C. Conditions and Completion mechanics

**1. Bluefen (Clause 3 / 6.3; DL 2)**
Seller: reasonable endeavours; consent "satisfied on delivery" of a written consent. DL 2 confirms: ~AUD 3.6m / ~30% of FY26 revenue; consent clause 11.2 has conditions in 11.3; **no final consent and no evidence conditions are satisfied.**
**Reject.** This is our single largest customer. Playbook requires an *effective* consent with evidence that the clause 11.3 conditions are satisfied, delivered before Completion as a condition precedent. "Consent-on-delivery" would let an unconditional-looking letter satisfy the CP while 11.3 conditions remain outstanding; "reasonable endeavours" is not sufficient for a material customer consent. Draft the CP as: unconditional written consent under 11.2 in agreed form, plus evidence satisfactory to the Buyer that all 11.3 conditions are met, with no amendment to the Bluefen contract.

**2. Riverlark (Clause 2 / 7; DL 3)**
Seller: ~AUD 3.2m outstanding; release "to be provided following Completion". DL 3 confirms **not repaid, no discharge of security in the data room.**
**Reject.** Debt-free/cash-free means Riverlark is repaid *at* Completion. Require: (i) current payout letter from Riverlark (dated within an agreed window before Completion), (ii) repayment direct from Completion funds per the funds flow, (iii) executed deeds of release / PPSR discharges delivered at Completion, and (iv) confirmation that change-of-control under clause 8.1 is dealt with. A post-Completion release is only possible with an irrevocable bank undertaking *and* Amelia Frost's approval – neither exists. Do not accept.

**3. Employee bonuses (Funds flow; DL 5)**
Seller: "a matter for the Seller", not itemised. DL 5 confirms AUD 420,000 of Completion-conditional bonuses are **not in the funds flow** and is silent on payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs.
**Reject.** If these are paid by the Company post-Completion, the Buyer bears them. Require either a specific line item in the funds flow (AUD 420,000 plus triggered superannuation, payroll tax and other on-costs – obtain the Seller's calculation and verify) deducted from the price / treated as Debt, or an express Seller-funded obligation with an indemnity. Ask the Seller to confirm whether "a matter for the Seller" means the Seller funds them; if so, document it.

**4. Funds flow generally:** The Seller says it "reflects the agreed price mechanics". Nothing is agreed. Review the funds flow line-by-line against Riverlark, bonuses, Sandbar and transaction costs before accepting.

## D. Specific risk matters

**5. Ironquay IP (Clause 11.1; DL 4)**
Seller: indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment, "considered adequate". DL 4: clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of *every* SOW3 fee; DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open but this is a Company ledger, not bank verification; **no receipt and no confirmatory assignment in the data room.**
**Push back.** The real risk is not the AUD 180k – it is that the Company may not own the SOW3 deliverables. Broaden the indemnity to cover loss arising from any failure of title to or right to use the Ironquay deliverables (all SOWs, not only SOW3), third-party claims, and the cost of obtaining assignment, while preserving the cure (payment of outstanding fees + confirmatory assignment before Completion, ideally as a CP or Completion deliverable). Treat the AUD 180,000 as unverified in both directions: request bank evidence of payments and Ironquay's own statement. Ensure this indemnity sits outside the general cap/basket/time limit (see A).

**6. Export/privacy incident (Clause 4.6 / Sch 6; DL 6)**
Seller: "preliminary operational matter… not expected to be material." DL 6: link sent to an unintended external address; ~1,240 records of personal information; unknown whether accessed; unknown whether notification required.
**Do not accept the materiality characterisation, and do not overstate it either.** Per the playbook we assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or quantum. Require: (i) a covenant to preserve all logs and evidence, (ii) completion of the investigation (access logs, link expiry/revocation, recipient confirmation of deletion), (iii) written updates pre-Completion and a bring-down disclosure, (iv) a specific warranty that the Seller has disclosed all known facts, and (v) a specific indemnity for loss arising from the incident (including any notification costs or regulatory action) outside the general regime. Delete "not expected to be material" from any SPA schedule – it is an opinion, not a disclosure.

**7. Sandbar renewals (DL 8)**
Seller: "ordinary-course operating costs." DL 8: three related renewals of AUD 110,000 each; the Seller does **not** state whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course – contradicting the Update's characterisation.
**Assess; do not accept the label.** Obtain DD-008/DD-011 together, confirm timing (pre- or post-Locked Box/Completion), whether any amounts are accrued but unpaid at Completion, and termination rights. No automatic Debt classification or price deduction per the playbook, but if any renewal is committed and unpaid at Completion it belongs in the Debt/working capital analysis.

**8. Office lease (DL 7) and Mossvale (DL 9)**
Both are low-risk on the disclosed facts (notification obligation, not consent; assignment restriction, not change-of-control). Verify the clause text ourselves rather than relying on the Seller's reading, and add a pre-Completion covenant to give the DD-007 landlord notification.

## E. Title, Tax and IP

**9. Title (DL 10)**
Seller: title "evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012". DL 10 itself concedes DD-012 is merely "the source relied on" and that the Buyer has not completed its own verification.
**Insufficient.** The share register is an internal document maintained by the Company the Seller controls. Require independent evidence: current ASIC company extract, share certificates (or confirmation of their absence), PPSR search against the Company and the Seller for encumbrances over the shares, Seller board resolutions and constitutional authority, and confirmation of no options/convertibles. Title warranties remain uncapped (see A).

**10. Tax / IP**
Seller: "settled under the general regime above." **Not accepted.** These remain OPEN. Nothing in the Update constitutes agreement. Respond that Tax and IP warranties and any tax covenant/indemnity are to be negotiated separately; do not propose unlimited liability, but do not allow them to collapse into the 20%/18-month general regime by default (which is exactly what the clause 12.3/13 catch-all would achieve).

---

## Summary of recommendations

**Reject and counter at playbook position:**
1. General cap 25% / AUD 6m (not 20% – no Amelia Frost authority exists for the fallback).
2. De minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000, first-dollar recovery.
3. 24-month general claims period (18 months unauthorised).
4. Separate Fundamental/Title regime: 100% cap, ≥6 years, outside basket/de minimis/knowledge.
5. Express, non-waivable carve-out for fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct from all of clauses 9.3, 12, 12.8 and 20.5.
6. Delete the "all limitations apply to all Claims unless stated otherwise" default; limitations apply only to general Warranty Claims and only where expressly stated. Tax, IP, Title, specific indemnities, payment and covenant obligations stay separate; Tax/IP remain open.

**Disclosure/knowledge:**
7. Delete general data-room and public-register disclosure (DL 1.1/1.2, Sch 7); require specific fair disclosure against identified warranties.
8. Delete clause 8.3 buyer-knowledge exclusion.

**Conditions/Completion:**
9. Bluefen: CP requiring effective consent plus evidence the 11.3 conditions are satisfied; not consent-on-delivery; not reasonable endeavours.
10. Riverlark: payout letter, repayment from Completion funds, releases delivered at Completion.
11. Bonuses: AUD 420k plus on-costs as a funds-flow line item or Seller-funded with indemnity; obtain the on-cost calculation.

**Specific risks:**
12. Ironquay: broaden the indemnity to ownership of deliverables; keep the payment/assignment cure; verify the AUD 180k independently.
13. DD-006: log preservation, completed investigation, updates and a specific indemnity; no acceptance of "not material".
14. Sandbar: assess timing and accrual; no automatic treatment either way.
15. Title: independent ASIC/PPSR/certificate/authority evidence; DD-012 alone is not proof.

**Process:** Reply to Seller counsel noting that no positions are agreed, the funds flow is not accepted, and our mark-up follows. Do not escalate for fallback approvals at this stage – the Seller's package gives no reason to move off opening positions, and the Disclosure Letter's own admissions on Bluefen, Riverlark, bonuses, Ironquay and title strengthen rather than weaken our hand.

Seller: "preliminary operational matter… not expected to be material." DL 6: link sent to an unintended external address; ~1,240 records of personal information; unknown whether accessed; unknown whether notification required.
**Do not accept the materiality characterisation, and do not overstate it either.** Per the playbook we assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or quantum. Require: (i) a covenant to preserve all logs and evidence, (ii) completion of the investigation (access logs, link expiry/revocation, recipient confirmation of deletion), (iii) written updates pre-Completion and a bring-down disclosure, (iv) a specific warranty that the Seller has disclosed all known facts, and (v) a specific indemnity for loss arising from the incident (including any notification costs or regulatory action) outside the general regime. Delete "not expected to be material" from any SPA schedule – it is an opinion, not a disclosure.

**7. Sandbar renewals (DL 8)**
Seller: "ordinary-course operating costs." DL 8: three related renewals of AUD 110,000 each; the Seller does **not** state whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course – contradicting the Update's characterisation.
**Assess; do not accept the label.** Obtain DD-008/DD-011 together, confirm timing (pre- or post-Locked Box/Completion), whether any amounts are accrued but unpaid at Completion, and termination rights. No automatic Debt classification or price deduction per the playbook, but if any renewal is committed and unpaid at Completion it belongs in the Debt/working capital analysis.

**8. Office lease (DL 7) and Mossvale (DL 9)**
Both are low-risk on the disclosed facts (notification obligation, not consent; assignment restriction, not change-of-control). Verify the clause text ourselves rather than relying on the Seller's reading, and add a pre-Completion covenant to give the DD-007 landlord notification.

## E. Title, Tax and IP

**9. Title (DL 10)**
Seller: title "evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012". DL 10 itself concedes DD-012 is merely "the source relied on" and that the Buyer has not completed its own verification.
**Insufficient.** The share register is an internal document maintained by the Company the Seller controls. Require independent evidence: current ASIC company extract, share certificates (or confirmation of their absence), PPSR search against the Company and the Seller for encumbrances over the shares, Seller board resolutions and constitutional authority, and confirmation of no options/convertibles. Title warranties remain uncapped (see A).

**10. Tax / IP**
Seller: "settled under the general regime above." **Not accepted.** These remain OPEN. Nothing in the Update constitutes agreement. Respond that Tax and IP warranties and any tax covenant/indemnity are to be negotiated separately; do not propose unlimited liability, but do not allow them to collapse into the 20%/18-month general regime by default (which is exactly what the clause 12.3/13 catch-all would achieve).
